verdict.rationale: SumUp's own integration options keep card capture on vendor systems: a SumUp-hosted payment page, a Cloud API flow where the Solo reader completes the transaction, and offline capture cached on the device. That architecture implies a reduced PCI footprint, but the evidence never mentions PCI, reader certification, or scope. missing for 10: any explicit PCI scope/SAQ claim, evidence of PCI PTS/P2PE-certified readers, vendor guidance on the merchant's remaining compliance obligations, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep my PCI scope minimal because card data is captured end-to-end by certified readers and vendor systems, with vendor guidance on my remaining obligations

citations.quote: SumUp hosts the payment page, while your integration creates the checkout and redirects the customer to the returned URL.

start a transaction from a Point of Sale (POS) running on any platform (Windows, iOS, Linux, Android, Web-based, etc.) capable of sending HTTPS requests and complete that transaction via a Solo reader
card data is captured and cached securely on the device, then uploaded later for processing and authorization
